review_notes: I read the whole file and checked it for repeated reasoning. Most near-duplicates are short: the ord_mul/ord_inv rewrites in exists_wronskian_family and evalVec_wronskian_family, the pivot/ratio setup in regVal_chord_eq_evalAt_wr and evalVec_wronskian_family, and the evalAt_add/neg/sub_of_mem trio. I judged these too small or too routine to report. The only repetition I think is worth reporting is the construction of a finite-dimensional intermediate field in absLogHeight_smul and absLogHeight_linear_le. I confirmed that finiteDimensional_adjoin_range in Definitions/Def_ModularCurve_JZeroHeightForm.lean only covers the range of one Fintype-indexed family. That is why both proofs re-derive the algebraicity argument inline. I did not check whether other files in the repository repeat the same block. The proposed lemma is untested and I have not compiled it. The saving is modest: a few lines in each proof, plus one place to maintain the algebraicity argument.

findings.problem: Both proofs build a finite-dimensional intermediate field E' as adjoin ℚ of a finite set. Each re-proves finite-dimensionality with the same algebraicity argument (every element of AlgebraicClosure ℚ is integral). Each then re-derives the generator membership facts with ad hoc subset_adjoin and Or.inl/Or.inr/insert plumbing. The same algebraicity argument is already packaged as finiteDimensional_adjoin_range, but only for the range of a single Fintype family, so these two proofs cannot reuse it. The repeated block is at lines 605-612 (absLogHeight_smul) and 626-632 (absLogHeight_linear_le).
findings.proposed_change:
Add one helper lemma next to absLogHeight_eq_of_mem:

theorem exists_finiteDimensional_superfield (S : Set (AlgebraicClosure ℚ)) (hS : S.Finite) : ∃ E : IntermediateField ℚ (AlgebraicClosure ℚ), FiniteDimensional ℚ E ∧ S ⊆ E.

Proof sketch: take E = IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ S. Use IntermediateField.finiteDimensional_adjoin with the algebraicity argument ((AlgebraicClosure.isAlgebraic ℚ).isAlgebraic y).isIntegral, and IntermediateField.subset_adjoin ℚ S for the inclusion. Finiteness of S is needed for the finite-dimensionality argument that the two proofs currently use. It is available here because the index types are Fintype.

In absLogHeight_smul, apply it to insert c (Set.range x) (finite via Set.finite_range and Set.Finite.insert). Then obtain E', hfd, hsub and derive hcE and hx' from hsub (Set.mem_insert c _) and hsub (Set.mem_insert_of_mem c ⟨i, rfl⟩).

In absLogHeight_linear_le, apply it to Set.range x ∪ Set.range (fun q : κ × ι => M q.1 q.2) (finite via Set.finite_range.union). Derive hxE and hME from hsub (Or.inl ⟨i, rfl⟩) and hsub (Or.inr ⟨q, rfl⟩).

The rest of both proofs stays unchanged. The imports are the same.
findings.benefit: The algebraicity argument lives in one place. Each proof loses the inline `set E' ... haveI : FiniteDimensional` block and keeps only its own mathematical content. A future change to how finite-dimensional height fields are produced, for example in the Height API, then needs one edit instead of several.
